Fit a Structural Equation Model by Maximum Likelihood

Source: R/fit-sem.R
fit_sem.Rd

Fits a model written in lavaan-style syntax to raw data with medfit's native maximum-likelihood engine, and returns a SEMFit object. The engine handles observed and latent variables, user labels, fixed values, starts and bounds, equality and inequality constraints (==, <, >, linear or nonlinear), and defined parameters (:=) with delta-method standard errors.

Usage

fit_sem(
  model,
  data,
  information = c("observed", "expected"),
  n_starts = NULL,
  control = list(),
  weights = NULL,
  se_type = c("model", "sandwich"),
  meanstructure = NULL,
  fixed_x = FALSE,
  sampling_weights = lifecycle::deprecated()
)

Arguments

model

Character: model syntax. Lines may use ~ (regression), =~ (latent variable), ~~ (variance or covariance), label*variable modifiers, start(), lower() and upper(), and the constraint operators ==, <, > and :=. An intercept is written y ~ 1 (alone or with other terms, as in y ~ 1 + x) and turns on the mean structure. A product of two observed variables is written x:m on the right side of a regression (canonical name m:x); ?"medfit-syntax" lists the supported class and each limit.

data

A data frame with the model's observed variables as numeric columns. Rows with missing values in those columns are dropped once (listwise deletion) and counted in n_dropped.

information

Character: "observed" (default) or "expected" information for the standard errors. "expected" is an error for a model with a product term that has an endogenous factor (the product is a function of another variable, so the expected information gives wrong standard errors); use the default with se_type = "sandwich".

n_starts

Positive integer or NULL: number of optimizer starts tried before the fit is declared failed (NULL uses 5). Retries use perturbed starts drawn under a fixed seed and never change the caller's random number stream. With a nonlinear constraint, which can leave several local optima, every start is tried and the best accepted one is kept (a warning says when the accepted starts disagree); otherwise the first accepted start is used.

control

List: options passed to the optimizer (nloptr).

weights

Optional numeric vector of non-negative case weights, one per row of data (NULL, the default, fits unweighted). The fit is weighted maximum likelihood on the weighted mean and covariance; the scale of the weights does not matter. Rows dropped for missing values drop their weights with them. Use with se_type = "sandwich".

se_type

Character: "model" (default) takes the covariance of the estimates from the inverse information; "sandwich" uses the robust sandwich covariance \(A^{-1} B A^{-1}\) with casewise scores (HC0-type: it equals sandwich::vcovHC(type = "HC0") per equation and lavaan's robust standard errors with sampling.weights, and is smaller than the HC3 default of the glm route by a factor that shrinks like \(1/n\)). Model-based standard errors are not valid under weights.

meanstructure

Logical or NULL. NULL (default) fits a mean structure when the model writes an intercept (y ~ 1, free or fixed); TRUE fits one regardless; FALSE fits covariances only and errors if an intercept is written. With a mean structure every observed variable whose intercept is not written has a free one, so a model with only free intercepts has the same estimates and standard errors as the covariance-only fit. A latent variable's mean is fixed at 0. A model with a product term (y ~ x + m + x:m) always fits the mean structure (it needs the mediator intercept for the four-way decomposition), so with a product meanstructure = FALSE is an error.

fixed_x

FALSE (default), TRUE, or a character vector of exogenous observed variable names. The selected variables (TRUE: every exogenous observed variable, product columns included) have their mean (with a mean structure), variance and every covariance with another exogenous variable fixed at the sample moments of the estimation sample (weighted when weights are given) and removed from estimation, as lavaan does with fixed.x = TRUE. The structural estimates, their standard errors, the degrees of freedom and the chi-square do not change; the parameter count and the log likelihood do: the log likelihood (and so AIC and BIC) is conditional on the fixed variables, and glance()$fixed_x lists them. Models whose fixed_x sets or data differ cannot be compared with stats::anova(), mbco_sem(), AIC() or BIC(). A (co)variance or intercept statement on a selected variable is an error (lavaan would silently keep it free). The fixed rows stay in the parameter table (fixed_x column, no standard error) but not in coef() or vcov().

sampling_weights

Renamed weights, the name fit_mediation() uses; the old name still works with a warning.

Value

A SEMFit object. With a product term whose factor is a regression target (x:m with m regressed on x), glance() reports the chi-square, df and p-value as NA with a note, and anova() and mbco_sem() refuse; see SEMFit-methods.

See also

SEMFit, fit_mediation()

Examples

# \donttest{
fit <- fit_sem(
  "mediator1 ~ a*treatment\noutcome ~ b*mediator1 + treatment\nab := a*b",
  data = mediation_demo
)
fit@defined
#>   name expr       est         se
#> 1   ab  a*b 0.3253207 0.08016376

# A treatment-by-mediator product: the four-way decomposition
fit4 <- fit_sem(
  "mediator1 ~ treatment\noutcome_int ~ treatment + mediator1 + treatment:mediator1",
  data = mediation_demo, se_type = "sandwich"
)
#> Warning: the model test is not valid for this model: the product 'mediator1:treatment' has an endogenous factor ('mediator1'). `glance()` and `summary()` report the chi-square, df and p-value as NA, and `anova()` and `mbco_sem()` refuse. The coefficients equal equation-wise OLS, and the sandwich standard errors (observed information) are unaffected.
decompose(extract_mediation(fit4, treatment = "treatment", mediator = "mediator1",
                            outcome = "outcome_int"))
#>        cde    int_ref    int_med        pie        nde        nie      total 
#> 0.04048833 0.07763088 0.22810575 0.32526471 0.11811921 0.55337046 0.67148967 
# }
